name: Burst-firing through four temporal coil pairs, 0.5 s per pair, 20 min (Tsang 2009 mood study)
summary: The burst-firing arm of Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2009: a 1 uT burst-firing field once every 3 s, passed through four left-right pairs of coils in boxes over the temporal lobes, 0.5 s per pair, 20 min once a week for 3 weeks. The paper reports lower depression and fatigue scores than with a sham field in 4 people per group; a random sequence given every 3 s lowered depression scores as well.
notes: Tsang 2009: 32 people in 8 groups of four got one of 7 field configurations or a sham field, 20 min once a week for 3 weeks, with 5 min of baseline before and after (p.1-3 [365-367]). Two boxes on a headphone frame sat over the temporal regions, four solenoids each; one left and one right solenoid were connected, and each pair got the signal for 0.5 s, 2 s per cycle (p.3 [367]). Table 1 gives this arm as burst-firing with an interval of 3000 ms and 3-ms points (p.4 [368]). One left-right pair is on at a time, and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. The paper gives neither the wiring nor the order of the pairs. The burst-firing point values were never published, so the project's rising sweep stands in: 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s), then a 3-s gap. The paper gives 1 uT and does not say where it was measured (p.1 [365]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT the scalp gets about 24 uT. Scores after/before (Table 3 p.6 [370]): depression 0.88 against 1.00 for sham, fatigue 0.89 against 1.08. A random sequence given every 3 s gave 0.92 for depression, so that effect is not specific to burst-firing (p.7 [371]). The results report no significant differences for vigour, anger or tension (p.6 [370]). Four people per group, post hoc tests at p < .10 (p.6 [370]), single lab, never independently replicated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not a treatment for low mood or depression. Not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated, eyes closed, in a quiet, dim room. The study had 5 min of baseline before and 5 min after the 20-min field. Fill in the same mood questionnaire (the study used the Profile of Mood States) before and after each session.
schedule: 20 min once a week for 3 weeks. To separate the pattern from expectation, compare blinded against the sham program and the random-field arm.
source: Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:365 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017627/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785 (ring order and the '20+2' notation) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, pp. 56-57 (CCW standard, 1-5 uT inside each solenoid) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/e809389f-805c-4414-8177-d0bf8d7127bb ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file, 3 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Martin & Persinger 2004, Neurosci Lett 366:226 (burst-firing once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15276252/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
